sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Mahakavi Dandi** (महकवि दण्डी), renowned master of Sanskrit prose and poetics.
**6th to 7th Century CE** (circa 600–650 CE), contemporary or slightly after **Subandhu** and **Bana Bhatta**.
Court of the **Pallava Kings** in **Kanchi** (Kanchipuram, South India).
**Dashakumarcharitam** (**दशकुमारचरितम्** - Adventures of Ten Princes), a classic **Katha** type of Sanskrit prose romance.
**Kavyadarsha** (**काव्यादर्श**), an authoritative treatise on Sanskrit poetics (**Alankara Shastra**).
**Avantisundari Katha** (**अवन्तिसुन्दरीकथा**), another prose romance attributed to Dandi.
**Vaidarbhi Riti** (**वैदर्भी रीति**), characterized by sweetness, elegance, clarity, and precise vocabulary.
**Dandino padalalityam** (**दण्डिनः पदलालित्यम्**) – Dandi is celebrated for his diction and word-grace.
High-yield topic for UP Assistant Teacher (Sanskrit) covering authors, texts, characters, and literary merits.

items.title: 1. Author Biography & Lineage
items.content:
• Grandson of **Bharavi** (**भारवि**), the celebrated author of **Kiratarjuniyam** (**किरातार्जुनीयम्**).
• Father's name was **Viradatta** and mother's name was **Gauri**.
• Orphaned at an early age; struggled through poverty before gaining recognition at the **Pallava** court in **Kanchi**.
• **Mnemonic:** **D**andi is **G**randson of **B**haravi (**D-G-B**: **D**andi's **G**randfather **B**haravi).

items.title: 2. Literary Period & Chronology
items.content:
• Placed traditionally after **Bana Bhatta** (7th century CE) and before **Bhavabhuti**.
• Mentioned by **Bana Bhatta** or referenced by later alamkarikas like **Vamana** and **Anandavardhana**.
• Flourished during the golden age of **Pallava art and literature** in South India.
• **Mnemonic:** **P**allava **K**ings **P**rotected **D**andi (**P-K-P-D**).

items.title: 3. Structure of Dashakumarcharitam
items.content:
• Divided into three distinct parts: **Purvapeethika** (5 chapters/introductions), **Dashakumarcharitam** proper (8 chapters/Ucchvasas), and **Uttarapeethika** (conclusion).
• Narrates the adventurous exploits, romances, and political triumphs of **ten princes** of Magadha.
• Written in **Katha** style (**कथा**), featuring fast-paced action, realism, and clever intrigue rather than excessive poetic description.

items.title: 4. Literary Style: Padalalityam & Vaidarbhi Riti
items.content:
• Famous praise: **'Upama Kalidasasya, Bharavearthagauravam, Dandinah padalalityam, Maghe santi trayo gunah'**.
• Master of **Vaidarbhi Riti** (**वैदर्भी रीति**), emphasizing clarity (**Prasada**), sweetness (**Madhurya**), and natural phrasing.
• Avoids excessive long-winded compounds (**Samasas**) compared to **Bana Bhatta**, making the narrative gripping and accessible.

items.title: 5. Poetic Treatise: Kavyadarsha
items.content:
• Divided into **three Paricchedas** (chapters).
• Chapter 1: Discusses **Margas** (**Vaidarbhi** and **Gaudi** ritis) and general poetic features.
• Chapter 2: Defines and illustrates **35 Alankaras** (figures of speech).
• Chapter 3: Covers **Doshas** (poetic flaws), **Gunas**, and word puzzles (**Yamakas**, **Citrakavyas**).

items.definition: Remember **K-B-D-M** (**K**alidas - **B**haravi - **D**andi - **M**agha) with attributes: **Upama** (Kalidasa), **Arthagaurava** (Bharavi), **Padalalityam** (Dandi), **Trayo gunah** (Magha).
Use **DKC** for **D**ashakumarcharitam, **K**avyadarsha, and **A**vantisundari Katha.
**3 Chapters** (**3 P**s): **P**ariccheda 1 (Style/Marga), **P**ariccheda 2 (Alankara), **P**ariccheda 3 (Dosha/Yataka).
**P-U-P**: **P**urvapeethika (Intro) -> **U**cchvasas (8 Chapters) -> **P**uttrapeethika (Uttarapeethika Conclusion).
Dandi loves **V**aidarbhi (**V** for **V**ictory in word-grace and **V**elocity of prose).
**B**haravi (Grandfather) -> **V**iradatta (Father) -> **D**andi (Poet).

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Prose Style with Bana Bhatta
items.definition: Students often think Dandi wrote in ultra-long compounds like **Kadambari**. Dandi uses **Vaidarbhi Riti**, which is comparatively lucid and clear.
**Bharavi** wrote poetry (**Kiratarjuniyam**), while **Dandi** wrote prose (**Dashakumarcharitam**) and poetics (**Kavyadarsha**).
**Dashakumarcharitam** is classified as a **Katha** (fictional romance) rather than an **Akhyayika** (historical memoir).
Although named **Dashakumarcharitam** (Ten Princes), the text actually details the adventures of **Rajavahana** plus **nine** other princes (total 10 heroes).
The **Purvapeethika** and **Uttarapeethika** are considered later interpolations by commentators to bridge missing parts of the original text.
Mahakavi **Dandi** is a stalwart of Sanskrit prose and poetics from the **6th-7th century CE**.
Fleurished in the court of **Pallava kings** in **Kanchi**, South India.
Grandson of the epic poet **Bharavi**, author of **Kiratarjuniyam**.
**Dashakumarcharitam** narrates the picaresque adventures of **ten princes** of Magadha.
**Kavyadarsha** is a foundational treatise on **Alankara Shastra** and poetic styles.
Celebrated for **Padalalityam** (**दण्डिनः पदलालित्यम्**) – elegance and sweetness of diction.
Advocates and practices **Vaidarbhi Riti** (**वैदर्भी रीति**), valuing clarity and precision.
**Dashakumarcharitam** is a classic **Katha** (**कथा**), showcasing realism, intrigue, and societal depiction.
Authored **Avantisundari Katha**, another extensive prose narrative.
Crucial for UP Assistant Teacher exam for questions on author lineage, famous quotes, and book classifications.

upscNotes.content: Memorize the famous kriti-author pairs: Dandi = Dashakumarcharitam & Kavyadarsha; Bharavi = Kiratarjuniyam; Subandhu = Vasavadatta. UP exams frequently test these exact pairings.
Do not confuse Dandi's 'Padalalityam' with Kalidasa's 'Upama' or Bharavi's 'Arthagauravam'. Examiners intentionally swap these attributes in multiple-choice questions.
Remember that Kavyadarsha has 3 Paricchedas. Questions regarding the number of chapters in classical Sanskrit treatises are standard in UP teaching exams.
Be careful with Dashakumarcharitam's structure: Purvapeethika and Uttarapeethika are frame additions, while the core text consists of 8 Ucchvasas.

keyTakeaways: Dandi is the legendary grandson of Bharavi, famous for **Padalalityam**.
**Dashakumarcharitam** is a picaresque prose romance detailing the adventures of ten princes.
**Kavyadarsha** is a monumental 3-chapter treatise on Sanskrit poetics and rhetoric.
Dandi champions the **Vaidarbhi Riti** style characterized by sweetness and clarity.
